terms.comment: The winner of a war or of any contest, with the genitive of what was won (victor pancratiī, Plin. NH 34.79). Of a woman victrīx; as an adjective, victorious (victor abībis).

terms.gloss: to be the winner, to take first prize
terms.comment: The winner as the one who takes the palm (see award).

phrases.latin: diē quīntō … victor in Capitōliō epulāberis. sequere
phrases.english: on the fifth day you will dine as victor on the Capitol. Follow me
give way to the one who resists: by giving way you will come away the winner

phrases.latin: victōrem forte gymnicī certāminis jactantiōrem cum vīdisset Phryx sophus, interrogāvit an plūs adversārius valuisset ejus.
phrases.english: When the Phrygian sage happened to see the winner of an athletic contest boasting too much, he asked whether his opponent had been stronger than he.
